summary.headline: ISGEC FY26 standalone revenue rose 4.2% to INR5,229 crore, below 7-8% guidance; FY27 revenue guided up 10-12%.
summary.overview: Q4 standalone revenue grew 16% and PBT 48% YoY, with a sharp Q4 recovery after a weak full year. FY26 standalone PBT was INR455 crore (up 17%), of which about INR80 crore came from Philippines items that management classed as non-operational, leaving underlying operational PBT near INR375 crore. Consolidated PAT fell 25% to INR154 crore, driven by a catch-up depreciation charge after the Philippines business was reclassified from held-for-sale to continuing operations. Net borrowings fell to INR476 crore from INR836 crore.

financial_highlights.change: within 12-13% range for third consecutive year
up from INR532 crore; more than doubled
includes catch-up charge on Philippines assets; YoY increase INR104 crore

segments.name: Manufacturing (Products)
segments.commentary: FY26 EBIT margin 12.46%; management expects 12-13% to be maintained in FY27 and sees the bulk of FY27 growth (about INR500 crore) coming from this segment.

segments.name: Projects (EPC)
segments.commentary: FY26 EBIT margin 4.58%; management targets about 5.5% in FY27 on older projects closing, newer shorter-duration orders at better margins, and contingencies. Projects growth guided at 3-4%.

segments.name: Isgec Hitachi Zosen JV
segments.commentary: FY26 total income INR672 crore and PBT INR103 crore; orders in hand INR763 crore at 31 Mar 2026. FY27 guided to revenue near INR700 crore and PBT above INR100 crore.

segments.name: Cavite Biofuels (Philippines ethanol)
segments.commentary: Commercial production from 17 Dec 2025 to 20 Apr 2026 on sugarcane, then molasses. FY26 reported loss INR295 crore, including INR170 crore depreciation, INR95 crore forex and ~INR70 crore interest; operating loss ~INR26 crore. Plant at 70-75% utilisation now, targeted 85-90%; FY27 depreciation seen near INR150 crore.

guidance_outlook: FY27 standalone revenue guided up 10-12%, with about INR500 crore of the increase from manufacturing and 3-4% growth in projects.
Manufacturing EBIT margin of 12-13% expected to be maintained in FY27 despite input cost inflation.
Projects EBIT margin expected to improve to about 5.5% in FY27 from 4.58%.
Export revenue expected to exceed INR1,100-1,200 crore in FY27; export order book about INR1,450 crore at 31 Mar 2026 and expected to grow in percentage terms.
Opening FY27 order book about INR7,000 crore after excluding INR550 crore of cancelled orders; INR1,400 crore of new orders booked in April-May 2026.

Philippines ethanol plant expected to run at 85-90% capacity for the rest of the year, barring 1-1.5 months of heavy rain; FY27 interest cost on Cavite Biofuels expected to be borne at group level (loans now from ISGEC).
capex_capacity: Capex FY26 INR153 crore, funded from internal accruals; capacity additions underway across most manufacturing product lines and described as on schedule with minor adjustments.
Board approved an additional INR25 crore to expand capacity at the Muzaffarnagar steel castings plant (approved 1 June 2026).
Some new capacity expected to come online in FY27 and contribute to revenue; it will add depreciation.
Cavite Biofuels (Philippines ethanol) commercial production began 17 Dec 2025; operating at 70-75% capacity currently, targeted 85-90%.
Philippines business no longer held for sale; management says a buyer is being sought but no specific party is in advanced talks, and no letter of intent is in place.
demand_pricing: Demand: inquiry pipeline and order booking outlook described as strong in both domestic and export markets; no impact from geopolitical developments on existing orders.

Input costs rising for steel forgings, castings, chemicals and imported materials, plus higher logistics costs and longer transit times; gas shortages raised fuel costs but manufacturing has not been disrupted.
Cost increases expected to be absorbed mainly through contingencies and back-to-back supplier orders placed after customer orders are booked.
Export markets: manufacturing presses sold in Southeast Asia (Vietnam, Thailand, Indonesia); projects work in Africa and Latin America. Southeast Asia and Africa are the main export geographies.
Sector demand: sugar, power, oil and gas, automobiles and fertilizers cited as doing well; paper weak; few new ethanol plants being built in India.
Export billing is under confirmed letters of credit in USD or EUR, with forward cover taken; projects generally run a cash surplus.

qa_highlights.question: How is FY27 10-12% growth split between manufacturing and projects?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said manufacturing should add about INR500 crore, with projects growing about 3-4%.

qa_highlights.question: Is the 12-13% manufacturing and 4.5% projects margin at risk from raw material volatility?
qa_highlights.answer: Manufacturing 12-13% is considered maintained via back-to-back supplier orders and contingencies; projects margin is expected to rise to about 5.5% in FY27.

qa_highlights.question: Why did manufacturing margin soften in Q4 versus Q3?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it reflects which orders were dispatched in each quarter, since revenue is recognised on dispatch; annual margin of 12-13% is the right lens.

qa_highlights.question: Why did Cavite Biofuels post high losses in a peak season?
qa_highlights.answer: Ethanol was stored awaiting government allocations for April-June and July-September; dispatches were minimal in Q4. FY26 operating loss was about INR26 crore after depreciation, forex and interest.

qa_highlights.question: Status of INR300 crore FGD retention money expected in Q4?
qa_highlights.answer: More than INR200 crore realised; INR165 crore remains, with about one-third expected in June and the rest by August.

qa_highlights.question: What is the breakdown of other income and forex in consolidated results?
qa_highlights.answer: Forex fluctuation of INR103 crore in other income, of which about INR50 crore relates to Isgec Investments Pte Ltd (Singapore) and is classified in other expenses per accounting standards.

risks_watch: Input cost inflation (steel forgings, castings, chemicals, imports) and geopolitical disruption affecting logistics and margins; management says it is absorbing costs for now.

Philippines business: unsold, classified as continuing operations; sale timing uncertain and a prior deal fell through when the buyer could not pay. Ongoing depreciation of about INR150 crore for Cavite Biofuels in FY27.
Cancelled orders of INR550 crore in FY26 and FY26 revenue shortfall versus 7-8% guidance.
Negative net worth at Isgec Investments Pte Ltd and capital deficiency at Bioeq Energy Holding; funded via group shareholder loans.
Export receivables and currency risk in Africa and Southeast Asia; company says no significant money has been stuck with African customers.
Watch Q1 FY27: FGD retention collection (INR165 crore), Cavite utilisation ramp, order inflow after INR1,400 crore in April-May, and projects margin progress toward 5.5%.
summary.management_tone: Confident on the manufacturing margin range and FY27 growth, but candid that FY26 missed guidance and that the Philippines accounting and sale are uncertain. Management was evasive on Cavite Biofuels EBITDA and on sale price and timing, citing accounting constraints and geopolitical fluidity.
